sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area
lecture_lines: Determinants represent the area of a parallelogram.
Vectors forming the parallelogram determine this area.
Zero area means vectors are linearly dependent.
animations: Draw a 2D plane with two vectors forming a parallelogram. Color #FFD700 (Gold) for vectors, #00BFFF (Deep Sky Blue) for area.
Label vectors 'v1' and 'v2' in white, area as 'det(A)'.
Show transformation where area scales by determinant. Use color #FF4500 (Orange Red) for scalar factor.
Animate vectors stretching; show area change dynamically. Keep labels consistent.
Highlight the connection: Det(A) equals the area. Flash area in #32CD32 (Lime Green).

sections.title: Framing the Linear System
lecture_lines: A linear system Ax equals b.
This is a combination of column vectors.
We find scalars to reach point b.
animations: Represent Ax=b as a combination of column vectors. Use #FFD700 (Gold) for columns, #FF4500 (Orange Red) for x variables.
Show b as the weighted sum: x1*col1 + x2*col2. Label sum clearly in white.
Display linear system equation Ax=b center screen. Highlight vectors in #00BFFF (Deep Sky Blue) as they assemble into b.

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation of Cramer's Rule
lecture_lines: Replace a column to create new parallelograms.
The area ratio scales the unknown variables.
animations: Draw parallelogram defined by column vectors of A. Highlight in #FFD700 (Gold).
Replace one column with b. New shape highlighted in #FF4500 (Orange Red).
Show the ratio of the two areas represents the variable value. Fade areas in/out for comparison.
Add explicit text 'Ratio = Area(Ab) / Area(A)'. Color: white.
Flash the formula result in #32CD32 (Lime Green).

sections.title: Step-by-Step Visualization
lecture_lines: First, calculate the base area A.
Second, swap column one with b.
Third, calculate the area of A1.
Finally, divide A1 area by A area.
This ratio reveals the first variable value.
animations: Start with Ax=b equation. Display vector b in #00BFFF (Deep Sky Blue).
Highlight column substitution process. Change column 1 color to #FF4500 (Orange Red) to signify substitution.
Final ratio calculation shown as fraction. Use #32CD32 (Lime Green) for resulting scalar value.
Show division clearly: x1 = det(A1) / det(A). Text color: white.
Highlight final scalar value with a pulse effect. Color: #32CD32 (Lime Green).

sections.title: Summary and Limitations
lecture_lines: Cramer's rule is an elegant geometric ratio.
Expensive for large systems, efficient for small.
Useful for intuitive understanding of systems.
animations: Brief recap of Cramer's Rule formula. Display centrally in white.
Show large 'X' mark over calculation for high-dim matrices. Color: #FF0000 (Red).
Fade to closing slide with conclusion. Use soothing #808080 (Gray) color for final text.
